evals.prompt: I have a small markdown knowledge graph living at /tmp/mgm-eval-fixture (registry file at assets/test-registry.json, graph id 'eval-fixture'). Can you audit it and tell me what's wrong?
evals.expected_output: A single categorized report of every schema/link violation in the fixture graph, with no files written.
expectations: The report identifies a missing required property (born::) on the Person page 'Bob Example'
The report identifies the single-colon pseudo-label 'Favorite Color:' on 'Bob Example' as report-only (needs human judgment), not auto-fixed
The report identifies the inline-bold-heading pattern ('**Bio** — ...') on 'Bob Example' as report-only, not auto-fixed
The report identifies the bold-markdown text ('**Bio**') as a safe-fix category
The report identifies the dangling link [[Carol Nonexistent]] as a safe-fix category (target does not exist)
Findings are grouped by category (all instances of one violation type presented together), not per-page (not 'here are Bob's 5 issues' as one bucket)

The report never surfaces a raw per-script heading or label (e.g. 'schema-lint.py output' / 'graph-link-audit.py output') anywhere — confirms findings from both scripts were actually merged, not that the report is merely silent about internals (non-discriminating in prior iterations; this checks for the specific regression it should catch)

The report flags that the bold-markdown safe-fix and the inline-bold-heading report-only finding both target line 5, and warns that applying the safe-fix first would destroy the heading-candidate signal before it's been resolved (the ordering trap documented in SKILL.md)
No file in the fixture graph was modified (audit is read-only)
The clean page 'Alice Example' is not reported as having any violations

evals.prompt: Please apply safe fixes to my markdown graph at /tmp/mgm-eval-fixture (registry at assets/test-registry.json, graph id 'eval-fixture').
evals.expected_output: The bold-markdown and dangling-link findings on 'Bob Example' are written; the missing-required-property and single-colon-pseudo-label findings are left untouched with a specific recommendation for each, not a bare list.
expectations: pages/Bob Example.md no longer contains '**' bold markers after the fix
The dangling link to [[Carol Nonexistent]] in pages/Bob Example.md is unbracketed to plain text 'Carol Nonexistent' after the fix
pages/Bob Example.md still has type:: Person with no born:: property after the fix (missing-required-property is never auto-fixed)
The single-colon pseudo-label 'Favorite Color:' is still present verbatim after the fix (report-only, never auto-fixed)
The response gives a specific recommendation for the missing born:: property and the colon-label, not just 'here are the ambiguous things, you decide'
The response re-audited fresh before fixing rather than reusing a stale prior report

evals.prompt: Add a new page to my markdown graph at /tmp/mgm-eval-fixture (registry at assets/test-registry.json, graph id 'eval-fixture') for a person named Carol Nonexistent, born 1985, related to Bob Example. Her favorite color is teal.
evals.expected_output: A new pages/Carol Nonexistent.md file that conforms to the graph's format contract on arrival: required properties filled, existence-verified bracket rule applied, no bold markdown, no single-colon pseudo-labels (including for the favorite-color fact), writer attribution set.
expectations: A new file pages/Carol Nonexistent.md (or equivalently-titled) was created
The new page has type:: Person and born:: 1985 as page properties
The new page has related:: [[Bob Example]] bracketed (since Bob Example exists in the graph)
The new page contains no '**bold**' markdown anywhere
The favorite-color fact is written as a hyphen-separated label ('Favorite Color - teal' or similar), not a single-colon pseudo-label ('Favorite Color: teal')
The new page sets the page property writer:: Claude (new page, whole-page write)
The response confirms what was validated and prefilled, per the skill's write output contract

Restore or leave the file as the skill wrote it after the run — do not manually reset it back to the artificially-aged value.
expectations: The maintenance freshness check (Step -1) actually ran its version/doc-currency checks rather than short-circuiting as fresh (confirm the transcript shows real check activity, not just 'state was fresh, skipped')
The maintenance-check state file's timestamp was updated to reflect this run (compare against the artificially-aged timestamp the setup step wrote)
The state file write happened only at the skill's own per-skill runtime storage location, never inside the fixture graph being audited
